pl-l4d20c1-d1e115.summary: States that the time for penance extends to the last moment of life.

pl-l4d20c1-d1e118.summary: Quotes Leo: no one is to be despaired of while in this body, since what is deferred from distrust of age is sometimes completed by riper counsel.
claims: No one is to be despaired of while alive.

pl-l4d20c1-d1e124.summary: Quotes Augustine on those who defer penance: if someone in final necessity wants penance and receives it and is soon reconciled and departs, we do not deny what he asks, but we do not presume he departs well; we can give penance, not security. Do you want to be free of doubt? Repent while healthy, then you are secure, having repented when you could sin; if you repent when you can no longer sin, your sins have left you, not you them.
claims: Deathbed penance is granted but gives no security.

pl-l4d20c1-d1e134.summary: Adds Augustine: there are two possibilities, you are forgiven or not; which will be yours I do not know; so hold the certain and leave the uncertain.
claims: The outcome of deathbed penance is uncertain.

pl-l4d20c1-d1e143.summary: Asks why Augustine said this, since penance at the end is called the evening sacrifice in the Psalm, more acceptable under the Law, and God is present whenever invoked, and the sinner lives whenever he groans and turns.

pl-l4d20c1-d1e161.summary: Answers that Augustine said this because of those who delay penance until the end and then seem to repent not from love of God but from fear of death, as if from necessity.
claims: Augustine's warning concerns penance from fear of death.

pl-l4d20c1-d1e167.summary: Quotes Augustine explaining himself: let no one wait until he cannot sin; let him seek freedom of choice, not necessity; charity, not fear alone. One who repents late must not only fear the judge but love him, since no one is saved without charity. If such conversion occurs even at the end, his remission is not to be despaired of; but since it is rare, one should fear for the late penitent, especially when children, wife, and the world call him. Since fruitful penance is God's work, he can inspire it whenever he wills and reward by mercy those he could condemn by justice; but it is most dangerous to defer the remedy until death.
claims: Late penance must include love, not fear alone.
True late conversion is rare but possible.

pl-l4d20c1-d1e173.summary: Adds that even if one so converted lives, we do not promise he escapes all punishment: he must first be purged by the fire of purgation, having deferred the fruit of conversion to the next world. This fire, though not eternal, is wonderfully grave, exceeding any punishment ever suffered in this life, even the martyrs' torments.
claims: Late penitents must be purged by purgatorial fire.
That fire exceeds every earthly pain.

pl-l4d20c1-d1e182.summary: Concludes how dangerous it is to defer penance to life's end. If true penance is had even then, it frees and obtains life, though not without some punishment, unless the groaning and contrition are so intense as to suffice. Though true penance is hard when pain binds the limbs and dulls the mind, late is better than none; penance at the last gasp heals and frees. The thief's penance was very late, but his pardon was not; yet he gave the baptized no license to sin and persevere.
claims: Late true penance saves, usually with some remaining punishment.
Late penance is better than none.
The good thief gives no license to delay.

pl-l4d20c1.summary: Teaches that the time for penance lasts until the last moment of life; Leo: no one is to be despaired of while in the body. Yet Augustine warns about deathbed penance: we give it but cannot give security; do penance while healthy; if you repent when you can no longer sin, your sins have left you, not you them. Why this, when late penance is called the evening sacrifice and God hears whenever the sinner groans? Augustine speaks of those who delay to the end and then repent from fear of death, not love of God; late conversion is rarely genuine but possible, since fruitful penance is God's work. Even then one must be purged by a purifying fire, graver than any earthly pain. So deferring penance is very dangerous, though late penance is better than none: the thief's penance was late, but his pardon was not; yet he gave the baptized no license to sin.
claims: Penance is possible until the last moment of life.
Deathbed penance gives no security, since it may come from fear rather than love.
Fruitful penance is God's work and can be inspired at any time.
One converted at the end must be purged by purifying fire.
Late penance is better than none.
